claims.text: The rider's claim is proven on the platform's own trace: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events measures 15.52 km against a booked optimal of 11.2 km, an excess of 4.32 km. That is 38.57% of optimal, comfortably above the 20% establishment test, and 4.32 km in absolute terms, comfortably above the 0.8 km test. Both limbs of POL-RD-01 pass, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The governing distance figure is the trace, not the trip record. POL-RD-01 says gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where the two disagree, and here the trace reads 15.52 km while trip_record.actual_distance_km reads a rounded 15.5 km. The excess is therefore measured from 15.52 km, which only strengthens the rider's position: the deviation is established on the trace figure the clause commands us to use.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and discharges it. The artifacts describe the same trip: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02803, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-18T16:05:14+08:00 matches the trip_record's trip_started event at the same timestamp. The excess of 4.32 km meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, and it is measured from an unimpaired trace: 122 fixes, 100.0% coverage, 10-second sampling, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0. The burden now shifts to the driver.

The driver's traffic excuse does not discharge the shifted burden. His counterparty statement says only 'Traffic was heavy so I took another road' - a general assertion with no traffic_advisory ID cited. POL-RD-08 is explicit that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden, and assertions that cite no evidence ID carry no weight.

There is in fact no advisory on file to support the driver. The traffic_advisory artifact for this trip is MISSING - status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with the note that no advisory covers the Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's external-traffic assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else; with no advisory covering the trip window, that comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight. The deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No rider-requested detour excuses any part of this excess. The chat log for this trip is empty - message_count 0, no messages, first_message_at and last_message_at both null - so there is no rider instruction recorded anywhere that could satisfy POL-RD-04(a) to (c), and no waypoint_hint exists to corroborate. POL-RD-04 is simply unavailable on this record, and no distance is excluded from the excess on that ground.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point rescues the driver either. The trip_record shows original_pickup, original_dropoff, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at all null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-apply POL-RD-01 against, so the booked optimal of 11.2 km stands as the baseline.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and it is not de minimis. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs. The recomputed fare on the optimal route is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.2 + 0.28 x 15.1) x 1.5 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.00 on-route ERP = 27.4420, against a charged_total of 34.44. The refund is 34.44 - 27.4420 = 6.9980, rounded up to SGD 7.00. That is well above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and at 20.3% of charged_total it is far below the 90% full-refund share, so PARTIAL_REFUND is the correct outcome.

The surge multiplier must be read from the fare_breakdown, and it is 1.5. POL-RD-02's notes warn that reading surge as absent where it is present doubles the refund, so the ruling must state the source: fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.5, and the recomputed fare above already applies it to base, distance and time. The rider's refund is 7.00, not the inflated figure a surge-blind computation would produce.

The ERP line is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and must not be added on top. The single gantry charged, CTE Braddell southbound at SGD 2.00, is flagged on_optimal_route true, and the trace passes within 7.52 m of it at fix index 14. Because the recomputed fare already includes only on-optimal-route gantries, POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding this SGD 2.00 again; it is itemised for transparency only. The rider's total recovery is the SGD 7.00 distance-and-time refund.

The deviation is MATERIAL as well as established: the excess of 4.32 km is 38.57% of optimal, and while that does not cross the 50% materiality line, the driver_profile check under POL-RD-06 is nonetheless worth running because the evidence is otherwise finely balanced on the driver's traffic assertion. On that check the driver's trailing-90-day deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 413 completed_trips_90d, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is available to the rider. I do not overstate this: the rider's remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial of SGD 7.00.

The rider's own profile does not weaken the claim. POL-RD-08's corroboration gate applies only where deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; here deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the gate is not engaged and no extra corroboration beyond the trace is required. The rider's claim is proven on the trace alone.

The trace is clean for policy purposes and no escalation trigger fires. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met: there are no gaps, max_gap_sec is 0.0, the sampling interval is a steady 10 seconds, and there is no 500 m straight-line jump. POL-RD-10(3) is therefore not engaged, and the rider's excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider asks the judge to rule on the merits and award the SGD 7.00 partial refund rather than escalate.

claims.text: The rider's own claim is that the trip ran 15.52 km against a quoted 11.2 km. The governing measurement under POL-RD-01 is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which the trace records at 15.52 km, and the platform's optimal route estimate stored on the trip record is 11.2 km. The excess is therefore 4.32 km, or 38.57% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass: 4.32 km is greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 38.57% is greater than the 20% percentage threshold. The deviation is established on this trip's own trace.

The driver's explanation is that traffic was heavy so he took another road. That is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and under POL-RD-13 it is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle holds no traffic_advisory covering this trip window: EV-ADVIS-02803-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload. The comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the driver's traffic assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver cites no advisory identifier, so this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and the deviation stands at the measured figure.

The driver's assertion that traffic was heavy is unsupported by any traffic_advisory ID. Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and has discharged it with matching trip identifiers and a threshold-meeting excess on an unimpaired trace; the burden then shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12. A general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge that burden. The driver has pointed to no artifact and no clause.

The GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 122 fixes at a 10 second sample interval with 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) fires: there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The trace is therefore fully usable to establish the deviation, and no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required.

No exculpatory clause on the driver's side is available on this record. There is no chat_log content at all: EV-CHAT-02803 carries 0 messages, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and no rider-requested detour can be shown. The trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The fare model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. The excess stands unadjusted.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier recorded on the fare breakdown is 1.5. The recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.2 + 0.28 x 15.1) x 1.5) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.00 ERP on the optimal route = (3.80 + 8.40 + 4.228) x 1.5 + 0.80 + 2.00 = 16.428 x 1.5 + 2.80 = 24.642 + 2.80 = 27.442. The charged total is 34.44. The refund is 34.44 - 27.442 = 6.998, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 7.00. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 7.00.

The single ERP line on this fare, CTE Braddell southbound at SGD 2.00, is on the optimal route: the fare breakdown records on_optimal_route as true and the trace's nearest fix to the gantry is 7.52 m, well within the 250 m match radius. Under POL-RD-09(1) that charge is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which includes only on-optimal-route gantries, and must not be added on top of the refund figure. The off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00, so there is no standalone pass-through correction to make and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4).

The excess of 4.32 km is 38.57% of optimal, which is below the 50% and 8.0 km material-deviation thresholds in POL-RD-01, so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not triggered. Even if it were consulted, the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 413, so no pattern is established under POL-RD-06 and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. The driver's lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure.

The rider's profile does not weaken the claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the 4-or-more trigger in POL-RD-08, so no additional corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required for this claim. The rider's other profile fields are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not relied on here.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02803 measures 15.52 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff (trace_distance_km), while the booked optimal distance on the trip record EV-TRIP-02803 is 11.2 km. That is an excess of 4.32 km, or 38.57% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (above 0.8 km and above 20%), and the trace figure governs over the trip record's rounded 15.5 km. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 122 fixes, a steady 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and max_gap_sec of 0.0, so no independent corroboration is required and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

No exculpatory clause applies. The chat log EV-CHAT-02803 holds no messages, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and no rider-requested detour is shown; the trip record shows no amended pickup or dropoff (timestamps and amended optimal both null), so POL-RD-05 does not apply; the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply; and the fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. The driver's statement that traffic was heavy is an asserted external traffic cause, tested under POL-RD-13 against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. The only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-02803-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; no advisory covers this corridor and window, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and the excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08. I name that artifact, its weight and its issue code as POL-GEN-02(3) requires: its absence is citable but it carries no fact, and it does not drag confidence.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run on the METERED fare model with the surge multiplier of 1.5 read from the fare breakdown EV-FARE-02803 (surge_multiplier field): recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.2 + 0.28 x 15.1) x 1.5) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.00 on-optimal-route ERP = 27.4420. Charged_total is 34.44. Refund = 34.44 - 27.4420 = 6.9980, above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and 20.3% of charged_total, below the 90% full-refund share, so it rounds up to SGD 7.00 and the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. The SGD 2.00 CTE Braddell southbound ERP line is already comprehended in that figure under POL-RD-09(1), because the recomputed fare counts only on-route gantries; it is itemised for transparency and is not added on top. There is no billing-integrity defect: the gantry is matched by a trace fix 7.52 m away, and the off-route ERP total is 0.00.

On POL-RD-06: the excess of 38.57% does not cross the 50% materiality line and 4.32 km does not cross the 8.0 km line, so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. The rider's assertion that the deviation is 'material as well as established' is rejected on that point for the same reason. The driver_profile check, run because the traffic assertion was said to leave the evidence finely balanced, returns deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 413 - no repeat-deviation pattern under POL-RD-06 - and the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and has not been used. The rider's own profile gate in POL-RD-08 is not engaged (deviation_claims_60d 1, below 4), so no extra corroboration beyond the trace is required.

The monetary effect, SGD 7.00, does not exceed the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue; that refund moves through the payment ledger against payment_status CHARGED. Two claims - one from each side - that cited the missing advisory EV-ADVIS-02803-01 without disclosing its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code were discarded at the citation stage under POL-GEN-02(1); the substance they argued is otherwise covered above. Both parties may appeal this provisional ruling once, within 30 days, under POL-GEN-04.

charged_total = 34.44

On that check the driver's trailing-90-day deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 413 completed_trips_90d, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is available to the rider. I do not overstate this: the rider's remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial of SGD 7.00.

The rider's own profile does not weaken the claim. POL-RD-08's corroboration gate applies only where deviation_claims_60d is 4 or more and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1 or fewer; here deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the gate is not engaged and no extra corroboration beyond the trace is required. The rider's claim is proven on the trace alone.

The trace is clean for policy purposes and no escalation trigger fires. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met: there are no gaps, max_gap_sec is 0.0, the sampling interval is a steady 10 seconds, and there is no 500 m straight-line jump. POL-RD-10(3) is therefore not engaged, and the rider's excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider asks the judge to rule on the merits and award the SGD 7.00 partial refund rather than escalate.

The rider's own claim is that the trip ran 15.52 km against a quoted 11.2 km. The governing measurement under POL-RD-01 is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which the trace records at 15.52 km, and the platform's optimal route estimate stored on the trip record is 11.2 km. The excess is therefore 4.32 km, or 38.57% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass: 4.32 km is greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 38.57% is greater than the 20% percentage threshold. The deviation is established on this trip's own trace.

The driver's explanation is that traffic was heavy so he took another road. That is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and under POL-RD-13 it is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle holds no traffic_advisory covering this trip window: EV-ADVIS-02803-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload. The comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the driver's traffic assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver cites no advisory identifier, so this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and the deviation stands at the measured figure.

ledger.claim: The driver's assertion that traffic was heavy is unsupported by any traffic_advisory ID. Under POL-RD-08 the rider carries the initial burden and has discharged it with matching trip identifiers and a threshold-meeting excess on an unimpaired trace; the burden then shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12. A general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge that burden. The driver has pointed to no artifact and no clause.

The GPS trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07. It carries 122 fixes at a 10 second sample interval with 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) fires: there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m, and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The trace is therefore fully usable to establish the deviation, and no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is required.

No exculpatory clause on the driver's side is available on this record. There is no chat_log content at all: EV-CHAT-02803 carries 0 messages, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run and no rider-requested detour can be shown. The trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The fare model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE, so POL-RD-11 does not apply. The excess stands unadjusted.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier recorded on the fare breakdown is 1.5. The recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.2 + 0.28 x 15.1) x 1.5) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.00 ERP on the optimal route = (3.80 + 8.40 + 4.228) x 1.5 + 0.80 + 2.00 = 16.428 x 1.5 + 2.80 = 24.642 + 2.80 = 27.442. The charged total is 34.44. The refund is 34.44 - 27.442 = 6.998, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 7.00. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a partial refund of SGD 7.00.

The single ERP line on this fare, CTE Braddell southbound at SGD 2.00, is on the optimal route: the fare breakdown records on_optimal_route as true and the trace's nearest fix to the gantry is 7.52 m, well within the 250 m match radius. Under POL-RD-09(1) that charge is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which includes only on-optimal-route gantries, and must not be added on top of the refund figure. The off-optimal-route ERP total is 0.00, so there is no standalone pass-through correction to make and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4).

The excess of 4.32 km is 38.57% of optimal, which is below the 50% and 8.0 km material-deviation thresholds in POL-RD-01, so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not triggered. Even if it were consulted, the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 413, so no pattern is established under POL-RD-06 and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. The driver's lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure.
